stem.text: People enter a stadium at a rate of R(t) people per minute, where R is a positive function and t is measured in minutes. Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( \int_{5}^{15} R(t)\,dt \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: It is the total number of people who enter the stadium from \( t = 5 \) to \( t = 15 \) minutes, measured in people.

worked_solution.text: R(t) is a rate measured in people per minute, so integrating it over time multiplies by minutes and gives an amount in people.
worked_solution.rule_named: units of a definite integral of a rate

worked_solution.text: The limits run from \( t = 5 \) to \( t = 15 \) minutes, so \( \int_{5}^{15} R(t)\,dt \) is the total number of people who enter the stadium from \( t = 5 \) to \( t = 15 \) minutes.
worked_solution.rule_named: integral of a rate is the accumulated change

worked_solution.text: The units are people per minute times minutes, which is people.

options.label: It is the total number of people who enter the stadium over the whole time the model covers, measured in people.
